Dialogue: I came to Elena's apartment downstairs, according to the address I got.
There's an old lady downstairs sitting on the bench next to an old cat.
I went over there and asked her about Martin's place.
Hello, do you know where Mr. Martin lives?
The old lady looked up and looked at me.
Martin? What are you doing with the old man?
I want to talk to him about something.
Are you a relative of his family?
Not exactly. I'm here to find him.
He lives upstairs, 302. I don't think he's out. Just go and knock on the door.
That old man's not a good guy to get along with.
He has a very strange temper. He doesn't talk to people very often, and others say hello to him, sometimes he doesn't care.
Yeah. The wife is early, the daughter isn't around, she's been living alone for years.
Doesn't his daughter live with him?
No. I don't know what it is. It's like they're not close to each other.
So what does he live on?
Yes. That’s what he used to do for a living. His eyesight’s gotten worse, but he still takes the odd job. He makes a little money each month tuning people’s pianos.
He’s blind. I don’t know exactly when it happened, but he can barely see anything now.
He’s an odd man, but he knows his trade. Some of the neighbors still call him when there’s something wrong with their pianos.
Looks like he's good at it.
Of course. If you do it for a living, you’d better be good at it.
She took a look at me.
Be patient with him, though. If he says something sharp, don’t take it to heart.
All right, thanks for reminding me.
I was just about to go upstairs, and the old lady stopped me.
By the way, what do you want with him?
I want to tell him something about his daughter.
You’d better tell him yourself, then. The old man doesn’t like talking about his family, so I don’t pry.
But it's not easy for him to live alone, even though he has a bad temper.
He’s getting on in years, he can’t see, and he still has to look after himself. There’s no one at home to help him.
Hardly ever. Sometimes someone comes by to have a piano tuned. Otherwise, he’s usually alone.
Well, that's all I know. Go on up.
I found an old cat lying next to me.
I crouched down, reached out and touched its head.
The cat looked up and looked at me and slowly fell back.
This cat's been here for years.
It's not good enough to feed it. It's like feeding it a little.
Yeah, like me, it's all old guys. That old man's daughter used to play with it when he was still here.
Then take good care of it.
I went up the stairs and found Martin's door number.
When I stood at the door, I suddenly hesitated.
I don't know why, but I don't think it's easy to say the next thing.
After a while, the door opened slowly.
An old man with white hair stands behind the door.
I have something to tell you about your daughter.
I followed Martin into the house.
There is a piano in the living room, and there are green trees around it, and the sun falls on the floor through windows.
Martin groped to the couch and sat down.
Did you just say you had something to tell me about my daughter?
I've been preparing for your daughter Elena's funeral recently.
The house was quiet for a while.
You know what happened to her?
You haven't spoken to her lately?
There's nothing to be sorry about. She hasn't been back for a long time. I don't know where she is.
He touched his knee and sounded a little tired.
I can't help even if she does come back.
I get by. My eyesight makes things harder, but I still tune pianos now and then. It’s just enough to live on.
The woman downstairs told me you used to tune pianos for a living.
Sometimes I get to work. My ears aren't broken, my hands can move. I can't do nothing.
I don't like it. It's just for dinner.
Did you ever teach Elena to play the piano?
Is it because she doesn't like it?
Maybe. She was always thinking about going out there, and she didn't want to sit here and practice.
She just wants to go out and see it.
Do you think she had a good time?
Didn't you come to tell me about her? Why did you ask me?
Because I think there should be someone she cares about at the funeral.
Well, I hope she has someone at her funeral who knows her and doesn't want her to be there alone.
Martin was silent for a while.
I just think that people shouldn't leave alone.
I found some old pictures on the locker.
The young men and women in the photographs stood together and one of them contained a young girl.
Are all these pictures taken before?
She used to be like that. She always laughed.
It was years ago when Elena was little.
Were you the one who took care of Elena?
I looked at the little girl in the picture.
What was she like when she was little?
It's lively, it's loud. It's not too quiet at home, as long as she's around.
Do you remember what she liked best when she was a kid?
Likes to go out. As long as the weather's good, I want to run.
Looks like she's always liked the outside world.
I thought she was too much of a wanderer, and now she's...
There's a woman in the picture with a young girl standing next to Martin.
She loved it when she was a kid, didn't she?
When I was a kid, I didn't want to.
I guess I'm growing up. Someday, kids don't want to be dependent on their parents.
Did you ever think that maybe she just wanted her life?
It's just that I thought she was too young to understand how hard life is out there.
So you want her to stay home?
I just want her to be comfortable.
But she probably doesn't think so.
There was a vase next to the cupboard with a few flowers that were already dead.
Do you remember what flowers she likes?
She said that the sunflower looked spiritual, and wherever the sun was, it knew which side to grow.
So, Elena, what do you like about flowers?
She liked a lot of things when she was a kid, today, tomorrow. I didn't care too much.
If you ask me what she likes to eat when she's a kid, I can say it.
Of course. She didn't like carrots when she was a kid. She had to pick them out every time.
When I grew up, I didn't know how to pick.
I'm looking at some dead flowers in the vase.
The flowers have to be changed more often, or they will soon be dead.
You can buy some new ones next time.
There's an old TV in the corner of the living room.
It looks like it's been on for a long time.
Yes. Sometimes the signal isn't very good.
Listen to the news occasionally, or put on some programming as background sound.
It's supposed to be quiet at home.
What about Elena when she was home?
She likes to watch all that stuff. Animated movies, ensembles, video games.
Well, I don't know much about those things. Sometimes she sits in front of TV for a long time and tells me what the people are doing.
Sometimes. She talks about her, I do mine.
I used to feel noisy, but I can't hear you now.
But I don't really like those shows either.
But she doesn't seem to like being quiet.
She always said it was too boring to stay here.
She probably just wanted to see the outside world.
There's an old wooden horse in the corner of the room.
The horse's color has faded, but it can be seen that it's been carefully guarded.
Uh, put it in the corner of the room.
Did she used to like to ride this?
Yeah. When I was a kid, I had to sit on it and let me push her around.
When I grew up, I stopped playing. Once I asked her if she wanted it. She said she didn't like it.
Then why do you keep it?
He reached out and touched the sofa arm.
Maybe it's a shame to throw it away.
But it looks very well preserved.
I rub it every now and then.
Can't you see? Can you find it?
I still know where it is.
Then you should be familiar with this family.
I've lived here all these years, and I can walk with my eyes closed.
I took a subconscious look at a wooden horse.
When I was a kid, it seemed like it was always hard to really throw away.
I don't know. I just feel that way.
The piano in the living room is in perfect shape and there's no dust on it.
Can't you do that without seeing?
You don’t need to see to do all of it.
Every sound has its own place. It's not very clear. It can be heard in the ears.
Martin gets up slowly and tries to walk to the piano.
He reached out to open the hype and gently pressed a few sounds on the key.
Have you ever taught Elena to play?
A little, but not very patient.
She didn't want to learn. I didn't force her.
What's the point of being angry? She doesn't have to carry on my work.
What do you want her to do?
As long as she can feed herself and have fun.
Why didn't you tell her that before?
Maybe it's because I don't know what to say.
I looked at the key and suddenly there was an impulse to press it.
Yes. But I've been playing this piano for years. Don't push too hard.
I gently press the next key.
The sound was ringing in the living room.
Of course. As long as the piano is fixed, it's a good sound.
Maybe when I was a kid.
Then you can try a few more.
I pressed a few randomly as I felt.
An unwieldy melody rings in the room intermittently.
Elena used to play like this?
She used to push the piano buttons when she was a kid. Sometimes when I fixed a piano, she came over and made a mess.
But then she stopped playing, and I felt a little less sound at home.
I looked at the key and didn't press it again.
There were several shallow marks on the wall next to the piano.
There are years and numbers written next to the graphs.
Why are there so many scratches here?
That's from Elena when she was a kid.
Do you measure her once a year?
Well, since she wasn't as tall as my waist, until she grew up.
Do you remember the last time?
Yeah. She didn't want me to measure it at that time.
She says she's grown up and doesn't have to do this childish thing anymore.
Do you think she's growing too fast?
But sometimes, I'd like to slow down.
I reached out and touched the mark on the wall.
These marks should be hard to erase.
I'm not going to wipe it.
There's something in this house that I've never felt better about.
It took him a while to talk.
Do you think a father should know what his daughter is thinking?
Because even the closest, it's impossible to fully understand another person.
What if she can't give herself what she wants?
At least try to hear her out.
Sometimes it's just to let people know what they're thinking.
That's easy for you to say.
He sat on the couch with his hands on his knees and seemed to be waiting for me to speak.
There's nothing to see in this house. It's old stuff.
At least there's a lot of Elena's life here.
Do you remember when she was little?
Can you talk to me again?
I want to know more about her.
Because I wanted her to have a better funeral.
What's the point of a dead man's funeral?
What good is remembering? She’s gone.
It still means something to the people who are alive.
I just think that when someone has lived their life with care, something of them ought to remain.
Martin was silent for a long time.
She actually liked me when she was a kid.
I used to walk her to school and bring her home every day. She’d follow behind me, talking the whole way.
She made friends of her own and had things of her own going on. She didn’t want to tell me everything anymore.
But sometimes I feel like she's getting away from me.
She said she was bored at home, living the same day over and over. She didn’t want to go on like that.
What did you say to her?
I told her life out there wasn’t all that great either. I told her it wouldn’t be as easy as she thought.
What do you think she wanted?
I just thought she should make the best of the life she had first.
But she may have had enough.
I'm sorry. Am I being too direct?
He kept his head down and kept it up later.
I was getting worse, and I couldn't see. She always said she had to go out and find work and make money for herself.
But I hate to let her go.
Maybe it's just that if she's gone, I'm the only one left in this family.
I know it sounds bad. She's got her own life, and I shouldn't keep her around.
Regret that she didn't leave at that time.
Sometimes I think if I could have said less then would she not have been so reluctant to go home.
I'm just an ordinary man. I don't know how to be a good father or how to get along with a grown-up daughter.
Because I think you've always remembered her.
You didn't lose the photos, the wooden horses, the marks on the wall.
She should know that you care about her.
I would like to formally invite you to Elena's funeral.
The funeral will take place in three days. I can pick you up if you like.
Yes. I've contacted some of her former friends and teachers, and they've all agreed to participate.
I want someone who knows her at her funeral to be with her.
He slowly leaned back on the couch.
I'd like to bring something, if I can.
What do you want to bring?
I haven't figured it out yet.
It's okay, there's three days left.
Let's wait till I think about it.
Can you tell me if she has anything to say in the end?
If I find out later, I'll tell you.
I stand up and I'm ready to leave.
Did you just say that her friends are coming?
She used to say she didn't know much. I thought...
Mr. Martin, you don't have to worry. She won't be alone.
I walked to the door and was ready to leave.
You too. Remember to take care of yourself.
And, uh, the flowers in the vase are kind of dead, so change them.
I stood outside the door and looked back.
It's just an ordinary home, but there's something I care about.
The photos, the horses, the tattoos, and the piano.
I just think that Elena girl should have lived here for a long time.
And Mr. Martin, seems to have been waiting for her to come back.
I looked down and looked at the list of invitations.
This should not be too cold at the funeral.
